items.title: Canonical ingress must be durably journaled before authoritative delivery
evidence: Production composition supplies StoreIngressJournal backed by Store.appendAuditEvent.
SQLite worker acknowledges append only after COMMIT; configured database uses WAL and synchronous=FULL.

A module-private Store capability checks the live worker database path, WAL mode, and synchronous=FULL; overriding the old public check method on Store(':memory:') does not grant a durable ingress capability.
CanonicalIngress rejects caller-supplied journals before creating or notifying a CommittedEnvelope.
test/platform/canonical-ingress-durability.test.mjs verifies memory-store rejection, arbitrary-journal rejection, commit-before-notification, and duplicate recognition after reopen.
Research cycle 134 added canonical_ingress_delivery_v1 as a SQLite outbox committed atomically with the canonical ingress event; recovery revalidates stored payloads before redispatch.

Crash-recovery test now proves pending delivery survives reopen and audit pruning, is replayed on duplicate submit, and is removed only after durable acknowledgement; delivered dedupe survives pruning.
Independent review found no transaction atomicity defect for fresh-format commit/ack, but identified unknown legacy delivery outcomes and non-durable Engine projection effects.
Research cycle 135 classifies pre-outbox rows as LEGACY_UNKNOWN, retains dedupe evidence, emits a durable uncertainty marker, and prevents unsafe automatic replay.
Engine projection checkpoint and outbox delivery acknowledgement commit atomically in canonical_ingress_engine_projection_v1 under BEGIN IMMEDIATE (cycle 147).
Implemented IngressVersionRegistry and versioned compiler/validator contracts (compileForVersion, validateForVersion, isVersionSupported) in canonical-ingress.ts (cycle 148).

Current C1 repair: only createCanonicalSolanaIngress can confer Engine-accepted reviewed provenance; direct CanonicalIngress instances backed by Store remain untrusted because their compiler/validator are caller supplied.

Current C1 repair: the reviewed factory accepts no caller compiler, validator, or coder; it constructs the fixed repository Pump compiler and DefaultTruthValidator before granting reviewed provenance.

Current C1 repair: submit snapshots caller-owned payload bytes before its first await and checks the digest after compile, validation, and before append; StoreIngressJournal copies and verifies bytes again after its durability await before serialization.

Current C1 repair: each ordinary subscriber receives a detached object graph with separately copied byte views, preserving decoded Solana value classes such as PublicKey and BN; one subscriber cannot mutate the committed bytes observed by the next.
Engine now verifies the reviewed ingress is bound to the exact Store used for projection; the Store no longer exposes its Worker message channel, closing direct postMessage acknowledgement bypass.
Current C1 repair: StoreIngressJournal accepts only the exact base class and freezes instances/prototype, preventing subclass or per-instance method replacement from retaining its brand.
Current C1 repair: committed envelope object graphs are deep-frozen (excluding binary views), and subscriber registration seals before first dispatch.
Current C1 repair: Engine occupies the terminal-delivery position; reviewed ingress has no generic journal ACK fallback and requires the outbox row to be absent after the terminal callback.
Store's general ingress capability exposes neither Engine owner binding nor projection load/commit; the Engine projection bridge is a separate internal module imported by fusion.ts.
Store.call rejects raw acknowledgement and projection-commit operations after reviewed ingress is created; unreviewed journal compatibility remains available for non-Engine test/adaptor pathways.
The C1 auditor now counts and rejects imports of the restricted Engine projection module outside src/fusion.ts, and imports of its underlying Store bridge outside the dedicated adapter.

restoreCommittedEnvelope validates both compiler and validator versions against the IngressVersionRegistry, failing closed with INGRESS_OUTBOX_COMPILER_DRIFT and INGRESS_OUTBOX_VALIDATION_IDENTITY_MISMATCH if unsupported or drifting.

test/platform/canonical-ingress-durability.test.mjs covers fail-closed compiler drift, validator drift, unreviewed version rejection, and successful recovery when historical versions are reviewed in the registry.
remaining: JavaScript does not provide secrecy from arbitrary code executing in-process: code that intentionally imports the internal Store bridge can access its opaque projection capability. The enforced boundary is repository source trust plus the C1 auditor allowlist, not a sandbox against malicious same-process plugins.
The production factory pins the active compiler and validator but does not yet provide a separately governed historical implementation registry.
items.nextAction: Maintain version registry entries as compiler and validator versions evolve.

items.title: Provider raw evidence is not uniformly wire-preserved
evidence: WebSocket path stores the received JSON-RPC frame bytes.

The alternate YellowstoneTruthBridge hashes a deterministic JSON projection of decoded signature, slot, and logs, explicitly labeled DECODED_PROTOBUF_JSON_CANONICAL. This bridge is not the live Feed.geyser ingestion path.

The unsafe rawWireBytes injection property was removed. Extra JavaScript properties, including empty, mismatched, or untrusted byte buffers, are ignored and cannot promote decoded evidence to wire capture.

Generic ContractCanary witnesses default to UNSPECIFIED for strings, objects, Buffer, and Uint8Array. Explicit representation labels distinguish JSON frames, canonical JSON, decoded protobuf JSON, and protobuf wire bytes; these are caller declarations, and a payload digest proves neither capture nor authenticity.

Defined RawPayloadEncoding and attached to UnvalidatedObservation and observation-factory. Live Feed in src/feed.ts propagates explicit RawPayloadEncoding across websocket (JSON_FRAME_BYTES), Yellowstone (DECODED_PROTOBUF_JSON_CANONICAL), and fallback logs (JSON_CANONICAL).

Research cycle 159 adds JSON_SERIALIZED_BYTES and DECODED_PROTOBUF_JSON_SERIALIZED_BYTES for locally JSON.stringify-serialized bytes, labels caller-supplied payloads UNSPECIFIED when no representation is given, and retains old canonical enum values for replay compatibility.

The live Yellowstone Feed and alternate YellowstoneTruthBridge now identify decoded-protobuf JSON.stringify payloads as serialized bytes; WebSocket frames keep JSON_FRAME_BYTES. This narrows false canonicalization claims but does not prove capture or bind independent Feed.accept fields.

SQLite canonical_ingress_delivery_v1 outbox persists and restores rawPayloadEncoding across crash recovery, tested in test/platform/canonical-ingress-durability.test.mjs and test/feed-validation-boundary.test.mjs.

The real Feed.geyser in src/feed.ts receives decoded SDK updates and stores Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(update)); research cycle 159 labels these as DECODED_PROTOBUF_JSON_SERIALIZED_BYTES without fabricating wire capture.

Research cycle 160 replaces the live Subscribe client response deserializer with a narrow @grpc/grpc-js descriptor using the pinned 4.0.2 SubscribeRequest encoder and SubscribeUpdate decoder; it copies the message payload bytes and decodes that same copy.

Feed derives signature, slot, and logs only from the decoder-produced capture object held in a module-private WeakMap. Feed.accept rejects caller-selected GRPC_PROTOBUF_MESSAGE_PAYLOAD_BYTES unless the capture object, derived fields, and exact raw payload all match.

The observation encoding GRPC_PROTOBUF_MESSAGE_PAYLOAD_BYTES and schema yellowstone-grpc-protobuf-message/v1 identify protobuf message payload bytes passed to responseDeserialize after gRPC framing/reassembly and decompression, not full network frames.
Canonical Solana ingress now decodes this schema from the persisted payload and independently rejects signature/slot mismatch before parsing the transaction's logs.

Capture evidence bytes are held in a separate private Buffer copy from decoder-owned Buffer views; Feed signature/slot/logs are snapshotted at decode time. Adversarial regression mutates nested decoded signature bytes and logs without changing evidence or the Feed-field snapshot.
Yellowstone reconnect backoff now resets only after a session of at least 30 seconds; short-session update traffic does not reset accumulated backoff, covered by explicit threshold tests.

Independent Astra review accepted the capture binding, byte snapshot isolation, compiler binding, auth/TLS compatibility, and scoped claims; it prompted the follow-up condition that a stable session must also have received an update so an idle watchdog close cannot reset backoff.
The full npm run test:all suite passed on the implementation snapshot: core 568/568, intelligence 562/562, platform 959/959, terminal 312/312 (2,401 total).
remaining: The independent reviewer did not run a live Yellowstone provider/TLS integration; no live provider capture has been observed.

Generic Feed.accept continues supporting other transports and legacy representations. The in-process module and runtime remain within the repository trust boundary; this is not a sandbox against arbitrary malicious code importing internal modules. Existing *_JSON_CANONICAL values remain accepted for historical compatibility and remain caller declarations, not proof that bytes meet RFC 8785.
No payload hash or encoding declaration establishes transaction authenticity, chain inclusion, or source identity.
items.nextAction: Investigate provider identity, authenticated/finalized inclusion, and cross-provider reconciliation without expanding this payload claim.

items.title: Current truth validator does not independently prove Solana transaction authenticity
evidence: DefaultTruthValidator verifies payload digest and metadata shape.
signatureVerified is strictly false; authenticityProof is explicitly set to UNAVAILABLE_OBSERVATION_ONLY; inclusionProof is explicitly set to UNVERIFIED_LOG_DIGEST.
schemaCompliant is strictly false for generic/test compilers and true only for the versioned Solana compiler with decoded events.
restoreCommittedEnvelope verifies that replayed or recovered truth evidence strictly matches authenticityProof and inclusionProof.
Dependent authority remains gated at C4 static ceiling; unauthenticated observations cannot transition to live execution or capital authority.
test/platform/canonical-ingress-durability.test.mjs verifies fail-closed truth evidence and authenticity unavailability.
remaining: Cryptographic signature and finalized on-chain block inclusion verification require external anchor or multi-source RPC witness before claiming live chain truth.
items.nextAction: Maintain explicit authenticity unavailability and keep dependent live authority gated.

items.title: Engine still owns Feed construction, though its journal construction now fails closed
evidence: RuntimeComposition records Feed and CanonicalIngress references, and runEngine constructs and injects them paired into Engine.
Feed provides isIngressBound(port: unknown): boolean to verify ingress binding while preserving private field encapsulation.
composePaperRuntime enforces that injected Feed is paired with its bound CanonicalIngress, throwing FEED_REQUIRES_COMPOSITION_INGRESS and FEED_INGRESS_MISMATCH on violation.

Engine constructor validates that any injected Feed is paired with an explicit CanonicalIngress bound to the exact same instance before subscribing, throwing FEED_REQUIRES_COMPOSITION_INGRESS and FEED_INGRESS_MISMATCH.
Validation executes before registering any subscriber on the ingress, preventing phantom subscriptions on construction failure.
test/runtime-composition.test.mjs and test/c1-negative-compilation.test.mjs verify matched, mismatched, and missing Feed/ingress pairings.
remaining: The C1 source/runtime auditor must independently enforce the reviewed factory boundary and terminal subscriber ordering before this defect can be closed.
The factory pins the current Solana compiler and validator implementation; historical compiler/validator code provenance and review-registry governance still require independent verification.
items.nextAction: Maintain verified Feed/Ingress pairing across runtime composition entrypoints.

items.title: Committed ingress delivery is memory-only and can be lost or partially replayed
evidence: SQLite canonical_ingress_delivery_v1 persists the committed payload and acknowledgement state in the same database as the ingress audit journal.
Recovery on startup and duplicate submit revalidates and redispatches unacknowledged rows; pruning retains unacknowledged rows and stable dedupe records.
Engine projection checkpoint and delivery acknowledgement commit atomically in canonical_ingress_engine_projection_v1 under BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

Engine is registered in CanonicalIngress's reserved terminal slot. Registration seals at dispatch start, and reviewed ingress cannot use generic journal ACK even if terminal setup is absent or incomplete.
Downstream Engine event handling is idempotent via stable event IDs in audit_event_dedupe.

test/platform/canonical-ingress-crash-recovery.test.mjs passes crash/reopen, prune-before-replay, replay, acknowledgement, prune-after-ack, crash after projection commit, and crash after in-memory effect before projection commit.
remaining: The physical auditor and recovery tests must enforce terminal-slot ownership, immutable committed graphs, and subscriber-seal behavior across async dispatch.
Engine projection capability remains a same-process internal module export; C1 enforcement assumes trusted repository source and the C1 auditor allowlist, not hostile same-process plugins.
Engine in-memory candidate/state effects still precede the durable projection commit; restart rollback is the recovery mechanism and requires the crash suite to remain green.
items.nextAction: Preserve atomic projection checkpointing across future downstream handlers.

items.title: Runtime telemetry requires authenticated attestation and a connected producer
evidence: C5 certify mode requires the fixed persisted artifact path with valid Ed25519 signature and pinned public key.

Implemented RuntimeTelemetryCapture (src/platform/ingress/runtime-telemetry.ts) bound to Store-backed ingress; captures V2 spans (compile, validate, commit, delivery), persists to SQLite before signing, and signs 32-byte root with pure Ed25519.
Implemented RuntimeTelemetryExporter (src/platform/ingress/runtime-telemetry-exporter.ts) in runEngine for periodic atomic publication and bounded shutdown drain.
Implemented verifyRuntimeTelemetryStoreBinding in scripts/runtime-telemetry-evidence.mjs; re-reads and independently verifies the exact unpruned SQLite audit row and spans.
Implemented AwsKmsRuntimeAttestationSigner (src/platform/ingress/aws-kms-runtime-attestation.ts) for dedicated AWS KMS pure Ed25519 signing with zero transaction/wallet APIs.
test/platform/runtime-telemetry-producer.test.mjs (10/10) and test/platform/aws-kms-runtime-attestation.test.mjs (11/11) pass with 100% assertions green.

items.title: Production dependency graph contains unresolved npm audit advisories
evidence: On 2026-10-08, npm audit and npm audit --omit=dev both reported 15 affected packages: 8 high and 7 moderate, with no critical findings; all direct runtime dependencies are included in the production install.

The installed bigint-buffer 1.1.5 is reachable through @solana/spl-token 0.4.14 > @solana/buffer-layout-utils 0.2.0. That decoder calls toBigIntLE on account-data slices; project paths use SPL unpacking in src/market.ts and src/risk.ts. GHSA-3gc7-fjrx-p6mg has no patched upstream bigint-buffer release.

The installed toml 3.0.0 is reachable through @coral-xyz/anchor 0.31.1. Advisories GHSA-82x6-q7mm-w9cf and GHSA-v5mp-jgw5-2x6j affect older toml versions; project source imports Anchor EventParser but no project call to Anchor workspace/TOML parsing was found.

stream-json 1.9.1 and uuid 8.3.2 are reachable through jayson 4.3.0 and @solana/web3.js 1.98.4. Inspection found stream-json parsing in jayson TCP/TLS streaming clients; project RPC configuration uses the HTTP Connection path, whose response parser is JSON.parse. Jayson uses uuid.v4, whereas GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq concerns v3/v5/v6 with caller-supplied output buffers.

npm audit's proposed fixes require semver-major downgrades of @pump-fun/pump-sdk to 1.1.0 and @solana/spl-token to 0.1.8; these conflict with the project's current Pump instruction APIs and Token-2022 support and were not applied.

The Solana Foundation states that web3.js v1 is maintenance-only and points new development to v3/Kit; Sylph imports v1 types and APIs throughout the codebase, so this is a staged migration, not a safe blind lockfile refresh.
remaining: No compatible, upstream-maintained remediation for bigint-buffer was verified; test candidate replacement or remove the vulnerable decoder path with exact malformed-account regressions before adopting an override.
Confirm current upstream patched releases and API compatibility for Anchor/TOML and the Jayson RPC chain; rerun security audit, lockfile integrity checks, build, and full suites after any update.
Plan and independently review an incremental migration from the legacy web3.js v1 surface while preserving Pump SDK and token-program compatibility.
items.nextAction: Prototype an isolated bigint-buffer remediation and trace package-level advisory reachability before changing production dependency versions.
